Theme

Latin word

rēfert

rēfert (meā, tuā …)

impersonal verb, with meā, tuā or a genitive

it matters (to me, to you); it matters (to me: meā)

In this lexicon

  • concern

    also used · classical · Plaut. Pers. 497: et tuā rēfert; Traupman 294, 302

  • interest

    also used · classical · Phaedr. 1.15.9–10; Sen. Ep. 77.20: nōn quam diū, sed quam bene ācta sit, rēfert

  • magnī rēfert: important

    classical

  • Nīl rēfert.: it makes no difference

    classical

Examples

  • Istae quid ad mē? — Immō ad tē attinent et tuā rēfert.

    What have these to do with me? — Oh, they concern you, and it matters to you.Plaut. Pers. 497

    In the entry for concern

  • ergō quid rēfert meā cui serviam, clītellās cum portem meās?

    then what difference does it make to me whom I serve, so long as I carry my own packs?Phaedr. 1.15.9–10

    In the entry for interest

  • quā rē parvī rēfert mē probāre cōgitātiōnem tuam

    so it matters little that I approve your planCic. Att. 10.10.2

    In the entry for interest

  • quōmodo fābula, sīc vīta: nōn quam diū, sed quam bene ācta sit, rēfert

    as with a play, so with life: what matters is not how long but how well it is actedSen. Ep. 77.20
